title: Local Organizations Benefit from Annual Fundraiser
paragraphs: Chris Banks, Shiela House of the Harwich Children’s Fund, and Weedie Tyldesley

The Guild of Harwich Artists’ Annual Ornament Fundraiser held during the Harwich Christmas Stroll and on the following weekends at the Art Gallery, was a huge success. Total proceeds after expenses was the highest amount ever for this annual event. This amount was split evenly between two charities selected by the Guild’s Board of Directors: The Children’s Center, 115 Sisson Road, and the Harwich Children’s Fund. Each organization received $1,374.50.

Thank you to all Guild members who created the beautiful miniature paintings to be used as ornaments on a tree or stand alone on a table or desk. Tiny gold frames held watercolor or colored pencil paintings, as well as small canvases of oil, and acrylic. So much talent – and so much admired by all the buyers of the little gems. There were many comments on their beauty and at such a bargain price of $15 each. “We appreciate all that is done for the children and are honored to participate,” said Chris Banks, President of the Guild of Harwich Artists.
Weedie Tyldesley, Abigail Newberry-West, The Children’s Center Director, and Chris Banks

“I bought a whole bunch myself and kept some and gave some as gifts. I just love them! The money raised will go a long way to help our children and families. We really appreciate the support of our community,” remarked Abigail Newberry-West, Director of The Children’s Center.
